chunks: That was narrated by Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu al-Mu'za from al-Halabi who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for a woman to take (payment) for the breastfeeding of her child for more than two complete years. If they wish to wean before that, by mutual consent, it is good. And weaning is the same as stopping breastfeeding.'
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum duration for breastfeeding compensation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the two-year period for breastfeeding is a maximum limit rather than an obligation, allowing for early weaning through mutual consent ('an tarāḍin minhumā'). This ruling, recorded in Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the flexibility in family law to prioritize the well-being and agreement of both parents, defining 'fisal' as the cessation of nursing.
